shortDescription: Ferroglobe NASDAQ:GSM fell 6.7% post-market Tuesday after reporting a larger than forecast Q3 adjusted loss and a 2.3% Q/Q decline in revenues, citing a difficult operating environment driven primarily by higher energy costs resulting from the Middle East conflict and excess ferrosilicon imports in…

and a 2.3% Q/Q decline in revenues, citing a difficult operating environment driven primarily by higher energy costs resulting from the Middle East conflict and excess ferrosilicon imports into Europe.
said it plans to close five plants and shift production to its most competitive facilities, with the goal of improving capacity utilization to ~80%.
The company said the plant closures, together with a 20% overhead reduction, are expected to enhance adjusted EBITDA by $85M-$115M at full run rate, with minimal changes to annual volumes.

Q3 silicon metal revenue fell 3.7% sequentially to $101.9M, with adjusted EBITDA of negative $2.3M; silicon-based alloys revenue fell 6.6% to $116.7M, with adjusted EBITDA turning negative at $2M; and manganese-based alloys revenue rose 5.9% to $114M, with adjusted EBITDA of $11.4M.

"Despite the negative third quarter adjusted EBITDA of $2.4M, we generated $5.6M of free cash flow with net debt slightly increasing to $42.1M," CFO Beatriz García-Cos said. "We maintain our financial discipline while we continue to rein in costs within our control."

title: Ferroglobe plans five plant closures, 20% overhead cut in profitability push
